nodes.text: Developers of TinyML systems have no standard method to measure and compare accuracy, latency, and energy across the diverse hardware and software landscape of ultra-low-power ML devices.
nodes.audience_note: Reader needs to understand what TinyML is and why energy is a first-class metric.

nodes.text: TinyML enables a new class of always-on, battery-powered smart applications by breaking the 1-milliwatt inference barrier; comparing systems without a benchmark stifles progress.
nodes.audience_note: Adjacent ML researcher may not know TinyML scale or why wireless comm cost matters.

nodes.text: CoreMark benchmarks MCU compute but not ML inference; MLMark profiles ML but models require gigabytes of memory; MLPerf inference excludes MCU-class hardware.
No existing benchmark jointly measures accuracy, latency, and energy for ML inference on microcontroller-class (sub-milliwatt) devices while accommodating hardware and software heterogeneity.

Can a single benchmark suite fairly and reproducibly evaluate TinyML systems across accuracy, latency, and energy, while enabling diverse hardware and software submitters to demonstrate their contributions?
Design, implement, and validate an open-source, industry-standard benchmark suite for TinyML inference that is modular, reproducible, and community-driven.
MLPerf Tiny defines four benchmarks with reference implementations, a two-division submission structure, and a standardized measurement harness for latency, energy, and accuracy.
TinyML: ML inference on devices operating below 1 mW, typically microcontrollers running 10–250 MHz with <50 mW power budgets.
Benchmark divisions: closed (fixed model, dataset, quantization type) vs. open (any model, training script, and dataset modifications allowed).

Four benchmarks selected to cover representative embedded domains: keyword spotting (audio classification), visual wake words (binary image classification), image classification (10-class), and anomaly detection (unsupervised autoencoder).

Measurement harness connects a host PC to the device under test via serial port; energy mode adds an electrical-isolation proxy and calibrated energy monitor; median of five measurement runs is reported.
First submission round (v0.5, June 2021) attracted five diverse submissions across ARM MCU, RISC-V MCU, NN accelerator, software-only toolchain, and FPGA platforms.
Platform power consumption ranged from µWatts to Watts; INT-8 PTQ was the most common numerical format; no submission modified the training dataset.

The diversity of v0.5 submissions is consistent with the modular design successfully enabling hardware vendors, software toolchain providers, and academic groups to participate in the same benchmark round.

MLPerf Tiny is the first community-developed, industry-standard benchmark suite that jointly measures accuracy, latency, and energy for TinyML inference across a heterogeneous hardware and software landscape.
Pre-processing and streaming inputs are excluded from the measurement window; closed division models are limited to FC/CNN architectures; the v0.5 evidence is a single submission round.
Future submission rounds can track TinyML system evolution over time; the benchmark can expand to new application domains (wearables, medical, environmental monitoring) and include pre-processing.
Future versions plan to include streaming inputs, pre-processing measurement, additional architectures (RNNs), and new benchmark domains.
